Bogdan Nicolae Marinoiu

Design & Engineering MSc student · Politecnico di Milano

I enjoy working on challenging projects where mechanical design, embedded systems and software meet. I am an MSc student in Design and Engineering at Politecnico di Milano, with a BSc in Industrial Informatics from Politehnica University of Bucharest and Erasmus+ semesters in Coimbra and Poznań. I completed two internships in Bucharest: VR and Unity at the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics, and CAD modelling in SolidWorks at CAD WORKS Intl.

Bachelor thesis

UPB · Supervisors: Conf. dr. ing. Constantin-Adrian Popescu, Asist. drd. ing. Alexandru-Ionuț Nicolescu

Design and development of a mobile robot integrated into the photovoltaic panel cleaning workflow

A low-cost mobile robot that cleans solar panels, aiming to reduce human intervention and water use. Full cycle covered: requirements and FAST diagram, system architecture, mechanical design and manufacturing, hardware assembly, software, testing and cost estimate.

Why it matters

up to 40%

efficiency lost to dust on panels (figure cited in the thesis)

Manual cleaning

High cost, risk (heat, cold, heights) and time, especially in large parks.

Objective

Less human intervention and water use, an affordable solution, and a working robot in the cleaning process.

Existing solutions reviewed

Serbot Gekko Solar

Switzerland · €93,000 · 1,000 m²/h · suction cups

Ecoppia H4

Israel · Helix technology (moves horizontally, cleans vertically) · fully autonomous, cloud-managed · waterless, soft microfibres

Design and build

Mechanical

  • 8 designed parts, FDM printing in PLA
  • Bambu Lab P1S and H2S
  • 250 × 250 × 178 mm, about 2 kg
  • Nut-and-feather joints, 15-tooth gears, airflow channelling

Electronics

  • TCRT5000 sensor, MPU-9250 IMU
  • DC motors, TB6612FNG dual driver
  • Li-Ion battery, LM2596 buck converter
  • RFID (RC522) and buzzer

Software

  • C++, Arduino-based
  • SPI (RFID RC522), I2C (MPU-9250)
  • PWM motor control
  • UML flow diagram of the logic

Cost estimate

  • Base workload: 1,176 h
  • × 1.2 complexity coefficient × 1.1 technological difficulty coefficient = 1,552 h
  • 1,552 h × 25 lei/h average rate = 38,800 lei labour
  • + 729 lei components
  • Total: 39,529 lei (€7,905)

Testing and validation

Functional, robustness, performance and integration tests.

Issues found and proposed improvements
